items: Bans and suspensions — FailBanned / FailSuspended exist as codes but nothing ever sends them; there is no account_banned table and no IP ban list
Failed-login lockout — passwords can be guessed at socket speed
Realm flags are static — a realm shows as online whether or not the world server is running
Realm population is always 0, and the character count per realm is always 0
CMSG_TIME_SYNC_RESP is never handled — the request is sent once and the reply ignored, so the server has no clock offset for the client
Latency is never measured, despite answering every ping
Account data (CMSG_UPDATE_ACCOUNT_DATA) is never stored, so client-side settings do not follow the account
Tutorial flags are always zero and never saved
MOTD comes from config, not from a database table
Banned-addon list is always empty; client cache version is a static config value
Logout is instant — upstream makes a player sit for 20 seconds unless resting or a GM
SessionStatus.Transfer is never entered; nothing moves between maps yet

The speed-change acknowledgement counter is sent and echoed back but never matched — the handler counts outstanding orders per move type rather than pairing each reply to its own order. Enough to know when the last reply has arrived, not enough to detect a client replaying an old one.

Per-observer field filtering is applied to both create and values blocks, and values blocks are broadcast to everyone who can see the object. Party-member visibility is granted to the object itself (upstream IsInSameRaidWith opens with p == this, and a quest log slot id carries no other flag) and to nobody else until groups exist; special-info is omitted rather than guessed. Both err towards showing observers less than upstream would, never more.
Create-block branches for Transport, HasTarget and Vehicle are unwritten. Living, StationaryPosition, Self, Position, LowGuid and Rotation are all produced.
Our deflate output is not byte-identical to upstream's, by design (PLAN §9 excludes compressed bodies from byte-exact comparison)

SMSG_AURA_UPDATE_ALL is sent when a unit first becomes visible, which is what makes a creature that spawned buffed — or one already burning when you walk up — show anything at all. 3.3.5a removed the aura update fields, so a create block carries no auras.
Only position, zone, map and orientation are saved — level, health and stats are recomputed from base tables on every login, so any change to them is lost
No name profanity or reserved-name checks
No declined names (the Russian client asks for them)
Character deletion is immediate — no in-progress state, no undelete window

There is no real Corpse object. A dead player's body is a remembered position, not something another player can see or walk up to — and the reclaim delay is sent to the client but never enforced, so reclaiming is allowed immediately.

UNIT_DYNFLAG_LOOTABLE is set on a corpse that has loot and cleared when it is emptied, and — since values blocks are broadcast — it now actually reaches the client, which is what makes a corpse sparkle and accept a right click. It is not yet rewritten per observer, so everyone in sight sees the sparkle rather than only whoever may loot it.
A creature's facing is server-side only. CreatureAi.FaceTowards decides whether a swing lands, but the client is not told — that needs the facing-target form of SMSG_MONSTER_MOVE.
Glancing blows exclude a pet victim upstream; pets do not exist here, so only the player half of that condition is modelled.
Threat has no taunt, no redirection and no aura modifiers, and MeleeChances has no aura or expertise terms.
Nothing checks that a player knows the spell it casts. There is no spellbook, so CMSG_CAST_SPELL is honoured for any id in Spell.dbc.
SPELLS CANNOT MISS, CRIT OR BE RESISTED. Every cast that passes its checks lands in full — no spell hit table, no spell crit, no resistance.

Auras apply, tick and expire, but only PERIODIC_DAMAGE and PERIODIC_HEAL DO ANYTHING. Every other type is applied and shown on the buff bar and has no effect — a slow that does not slow. No stacking, no charges, no dispel, no procs.
A creature's spell damage is not rescaled by its level. Upstream multiplies by the ratio of the creature's base damage to the spell's for spells flagged to scale.
Nothing interrupts a cast. Moving, taking damage and dying all leave the bar running; only CMSG_CANCEL_CAST ends one early.

Experience is paid in full to everyone on the threat list, not split. Group splitting needs groups; paying each participant the whole amount errs towards over-rewarding, which is visible, rather than silently paying nobody.
The content level comes from the creature's template expansion, not its zone. Upstream uses the zone, so a classic creature standing in Outland pays classic rates here and Outland rates there.
There is no rested experience, no recruit-a-friend and no group rate. All three are multipliers on top of a figure that is computed correctly.
They do nothing. No opening, looting, using, or trapping — a gameobject stands where its row puts it and can be looked at.
The 32 data0..data31 columns are not read, so nothing knows what a door opens with or where a teleporter goes
gameobject_template_addon is not read, so per-spawn faction and flag overrides are missing
Three templates carry size = 0 and 11 spawns use them; they are drawn at nothing. Upstream does the same, so it is reproduced rather than corrected — but it looks like a bug when found.
1,193 spawns have no display id. These are invisible triggers and upstream creates them too, but each still costs a create block to a client that will never see anything.
Rotation is computed once at spawn and is not an update field
Movement ignores collision entirely — a creature walks through walls, trees and each other, because there is no pathfinding yet

Health uses no per-rank rate. Upstream multiplies by Rate.Creature.*.HP from the config; all five default to 1.0 and there is no config system for them, so they are omitted rather than hard-coded to a number that would look deliberate.
creature_addon and creature_equip_template are not read, so no creature has visible weapons or its spawn auras

The damage formula follows our DATA, not the C++ checkout: the current tree scales damage_base by a BaseVariance column our dump predates, so the older mindmg/maxdmg/dmg_multiplier form is used instead.
No aura or item contributes to damage, because neither exists — upstream runs the result through four modifier layers that are all identity without them
Difficulty entries (difficulty_entry_1..3) are ignored; every creature is built from its normal-mode template
phaseMask is loaded and stored but never checked — everything is visible to everyone

Links are not read from .mmtile and must not be — the file reserves MaxLinkCount links' worth of space, but Detour builds them when a tile is added, so what is on disk is uninitialised. Anything that starts reading them is reading noise.

The under-the-world threshold (25 yards) is a judgement, not a measurement. It has been exercised by the gate walking on open ground, not by a real client in a city or a cave — the false-positive rate is unknown.
Vmap tiles are loaded on demand and never unloaded, the same gap grid loading has.
CollectCandidates allocates a List<uint> per group per ray. Fine for the tests, not for a tick.
The single-child (BVH2) branch of the BIH walk is written from the C++ and never observed firing in a test.

132 of 436 sampled model groups carry an all-zero bounding box while holding real geometry. A zero box means "not recorded", not "empty" — anything that culls by it must not conclude the group is nowhere.
Model liquids parse but are unused; the tileless single-height form was not seen in the sampled files.
Off-mesh connections are exercised by exactly one tile in the entire extraction (5622031.mmtile, Blade's Edge Arena, 2 connections).
Only 9 of 109 DBC stores are loaded
.map flight bounds are parsed past but discarded
Terrain holes are implemented but never exercised by a test against a known hole
World tables are imported by piping vendored .sql dumps — there is no real importer, no schema mapping and no type cleanup. 12 of upstream's 309 tables are vendored so far.
world structure is upstream's verbatim, not a schema we own. PLAN §5.2 wants cleaned types and names with columns and semantics preserved — that belongs in WowEmu.Data.Import.
Nothing creates an item yet. The store, the object and the query response exist; there are no bags to put one in, so no player owns anything.
No random properties, no enchantments, no gems — the fields are on the object and nothing writes them.
Item duration is copied from the template and never counts down.
locales_item is not read, so every tooltip is English whatever the client asked for.
BuyPrice is a bigint in the table and an int32 on the wire. Following the C++ struct rather than the column; no real row is anywhere near the boundary.
No bank, no keyring, no buyback and no bag families. The slots exist in the array and nothing moves anything into them.
Soulbinding, unique constraints and item limit categories all pass — nothing is ever bound, and a player can carry two of a unique item. Weapon and armour proficiency IS enforced now.
Only the five attributes are applied from an item. Ratings, resistances and spell power are read and ignored.
Armour is the sum of the equipped items' columns and nothing else — agility's contribution needs the gt* DBCs.
The inventory is saved on logout and on a dropped connection, never periodically. A server crash loses everything since login, exactly as it does for position.
SMSG_ITEM_PUSH_RESULT is written and tested but nothing sends it yet — the "you received" toast arrives with loot.
Values blocks go only to the owner. Other players see neither equipment nor health change, because the dirty mask does not know which fields are private.
No groups, so no round-robin, no need/greed rolls, no master looter and no free-for-all. Whoever is top of the threat list owns the corpse outright.
QUEST DROPS ARE ROLLED AND SHOWN TO EVERYONE. The flag is read and nothing filters on it, because nobody has any quests to filter against.
Only creature corpses. Skinning, pickpocketing, fishing, disenchanting, gameobject and item loot all exist in the client and none of them are answered.
The conditions system is not read, so a row gated on reputation or a quest state drops unconditionally.
Drop rates are taken at face value — upstream scales them per item quality from its configuration, and all those rates are 1.0 by default.
A looted corpse is not despawned early. The corpse delay owns that, so an emptied corpse lies there for the rest of it.

PrevQuestId is now enforced, in its positive and negative forms. ExclusiveGroup and the multi-prerequisite list the C++ builds from it are still not read, so a quest gated on a group is admitted on its first prerequisite alone. NextQuestId is read and unused.
No timed quests, no area-trigger objectives, no escorts and no event objectives. Only creature kills and carried items count.
Reputation and skill requirements pass, and reputation, spell and title rewards are not paid.
Only creatures give quests — gameobject_queststarter and _questender are not read.
Daily and weekly quests do not reset; a repeatable one can be taken again immediately.

An autocomplete quest (Flags 0x00010000, or Method 0) opens the details window instead of the request-items one. It is still completable — accept, then hand in — but the first click shows the wrong dialog. The blizzlike path ends in RewardQuest paying out a quest that was never in the log, which is not built.

A quest whose SpecialFlags carry EXPLORATION_OR_EVENT, and the two that require player kills, are now permanently incomplete rather than wrongly complete. What would finish them is a script and a PvP-kill hook, neither of which exists.

The questgiver marker is a port of GetQuestDialogStatus, but the low-level variants use a hardcoded Quests.LowLevelHideDiff of 4 and the reputation-flavoured statuses (AVAILABLE_REP, REWARD_REP) are never produced, because repeatable and daily handling is not there. Conditions (CONDITION_SOURCE_TYPE_QUEST_AVAILABLE) are not consulted either.

Still unhandled: CMSG_QUEST_POI_QUERY (the map markers for objectives), CMSG_QUERY_QUESTS_COMPLETED (the completed-quest bitmask the client asks for on login), CMSG_QUEST_CONFIRM_ACCEPT and CMSG_PUSHQUESTTOPARTY (party quest sharing). None blocks the single-player loop; the first two mean an empty quest-tracker map and no credit for already-completed quests in the client's own UI.
Flight masters, bankers, innkeepers, auctioneers and stable masters still do nothing: the gossip line appears and clicking it closes the window. Trainers now work.
Every vendor has infinite stock. maxcount and the restock timer are read and ignored.
Items with an extended cost — honour, arena points, tokens — are listed and refused, because the cost is a row in a DBC nothing reads.
No buyback, no repair, and no reputation discount on prices.

Only the first of an npc_text row's eight text slots is read, and only the male variant. The conditions system that picks between a menu's several texts is not implemented, so the first is always used.
Everything is saved on logout and on a dropped connection, never periodically. A server crash loses the whole session — position, bags, quests, money and experience alike.

Confirming against a real 3.3.5a client is only just starting, and the first thing it found was an empty quest log — SMSG_QUEST_QUERY_RESPONSE was never answered. Five headless gates prove the server is self-consistent; none of them can prove the client agrees.
No spell ranks. A higher rank does not supersede a lower one, so a player who learns rank 2 keeps rank 1 in the book as well.

Skills gain through COMBAT only — weapon skill and defence go up from melee exchanges. Crafting, gathering and fishing gains are not written, because there is nothing to call them: no crafting, no gathering, no fishing. Skill tiers (apprentice through master) are read but never stepped up, so a profession cannot pass its first tier's ceiling.
No talents, no specs, no glyphs.
Spell cooldowns do not survive a logout — SMSG_INITIAL_SPELLS always reports none.

remember: Session handlers that await resume on the tick, but nothing ENFORCES it: a future handler that writes ConfigureAwait(false) would silently resume on the thread pool and touch a Player from outside its loop. TickScheduler.AssertOwnerThread exists for exactly this and is not yet wired in.

THE TWO REFERENCE TREES ARE AT DIFFERENT POINTS IN AZEROTHCORE'S HISTORY, and creature spawning is the first place it bites. The C++ reads creature models from a creature_template_model table; the vendored database still has modelid1..4. Ours follows the DATA. Read the C++ for behaviour, but check the dump before trusting a column name.
Both reference trees (azerothcore-wotlk, database-wotlk) have no git root — updating means re-cloning.

sql/world/ is now ~65 MB: item_template (14 MB), quest_template (13 MB), creature (12 MB), creature_loot_template (9 MB), creature_template (7.6 MB), gameobject (7 MB), npc_text (2.6 MB). The vendoring rule says a fresh clone must be able to start, and that is the price.
data/ is 3 GB of extracted client data and is not committed; a fresh clone needs the extractors run again.
sql/world/ redistributes AGPL-3.0 content from AzerothCore's database. Deliberate — but it is a licence obligation worth being aware of.

FIVE TABLES NOW OVERLOAD A COLUMN'S SIGN: creature_loot_template's mincountOrRef, npc_vendor's item, npc_trainer's SpellID, quest_template's RequiredNpcOrGo (gameobject) and RewardOrRequiredMoney (a cost). Read any unsigned and the failure is silent in most cases. Check the column's signedness before writing the reader.

FIVE TABLES NOW DIVERGE BETWEEN THE TWO REFERENCE TREES: creature_template_model vs modelid1..4, game_graveyard vs game_graveyard_zone, AreaDescription vs EndText, playercreateinfo_spell vs playercreateinfo_spell_custom (the newer C++ reads the _custom table, which our dump leaves empty), and quest_template.SpecialFlags (tinyint, in quest_template) vs quest_template_addon.SpecialFlags (int unsigned, whose allowed bits run past 255). Read the C++ for behaviour and the dump for column names — and for column WIDTHS.

A QUEST HAS TWO INDEPENDENT FLAG COLUMNS and their bits collide numerically. Repeatable and Monthly are SpecialFlags (0x0001 / 0x0010); AutoComplete is Flags 0x00010000 and HiddenRewards is Flags 0x0200. Reading one column with the other's constants compiles, runs, and silently answers a different question about every quest in the game. The same trap sits on the wire: QuestGiverStatus (0/1/2/5/8/9/10, the mark over the NPC) is NOT QuestMenuItem::QuestIcon (0/2/4, which half of the window a line files under), and both are written as a uint32.

NORTHSHIRE IS ONE LONG CHAIN. quest_template.PrevQuestId gates nearly every quest in the human start zone: 783 -> 5261 -> 33, and 783 -> 7 -> 15 -> 21. Any harness that takes a quest there has to walk the chain, and two quests picked at random usually cannot be held at the same time.

ACCEPTING A QUEST SENDS THE CLIENT NO QUEST PACKET. Player::AddQuest writes the five log-slot words and calls SendQuestUpdate, which despite its name sends nothing — it only re-evaluates area auras. CompleteQuest then sets the state word. SMSG_QUESTUPDATE_COMPLETE has exactly one caller in all of AzerothCore, AreaExploredOrEventHappens; sending it on accept hands the client a completion for a quest it is still building a log row for. Before adding a packet to a path, grep for the sender in the C++ and check how many callers it really has.

THE QUEST MENU ICON DECIDES WHICH OPCODE THE CLIENT SENDS BACK. An 'active' line (icon 4) is answered with CMSG_QUESTGIVER_COMPLETE_QUEST and an 'available' one (icon 2) with CMSG_QUESTGIVER_QUERY_QUEST. Get the icon wrong and the two halves of the conversation end up on different opcodes, which looks like a broken window rather than a wrong icon.

AN AUTO-ACCEPT QUEST IS TAKEN BY THE SERVER, NOT THE CLIENT. QUEST_FLAGS_AUTO_ACCEPT (Flags 0x00080000, NOT the SpecialFlags 0x0004 bit of the same name) is read by the 3.3.5a client too: it treats the quest as already taken the moment the details window opens and never sends CMSG_QUESTGIVER_ACCEPT_QUEST. The server must add it itself, and on BOTH routes into that window - the C++ repeats the call in SendPreparedQuest and HandleQuestgiverQueryQuestOpcode. Quest 783 'A Threat Within' is one, so this breaks the human starting zone outright.

A HARNESS THAT SENDS A PACKET THE REAL CLIENT WOULD NOT is worse than no harness. m6_quest sent an accept for an auto-accept quest and stayed green while the game was unplayable, and it asserted on an SMSG_QUESTUPDATE_COMPLETE that AzerothCore never sends, which kept a spurious packet alive. When a gate passes and the client disagrees, suspect the gate first: ask what the client would NOT do, not only what it would.

QUEST FLAGS COME FROM TWO TABLES AND ARE MERGED AT LOAD. Quest::Quest reads quest_template.Flags, then LoadQuestTemplateAddon ORs QUEST_FLAGS_AUTO_ACCEPT in for any quest whose quest_template_addon.SpecialFlags has 0x0004 (Quests.IgnoreAutoAccept, default 0, strips it instead). 177 of the 9464 vendored quests end up auto-accept, including the whole Northshire chain 783 -> 5261 -> 7. Reading either column alone gets a different answer.

THE CLIENT ASKS THE SERVER TO CLOSE ITS OWN WINDOWS. CMSG_QUESTGIVER_CANCEL is sent when a quest dialog is dismissed and the window stays on screen until SMSG_GOSSIP_COMPLETE comes back; HandleQuestgiverCancel is that one line and nothing else. When some piece of client UI 'does not react', diff the handled CMSG list against Opcodes.cpp before reading packet layouts -- an unhandled opcode is silent on both ends.

sets.by: generate_random_vectors.sh — SFMT + libstdc++ in a gcc container

why: AzerothCore does not roll its own distributions — it feeds SFMT into libstdc++'s uniform_int_distribution and uniform_real_distribution. Those consume a SPECIFIC number of 32-bit draws: the integer one rejection-samples, frand takes one and rand_norm takes two. An implementation that gets the draw count wrong still produces perfectly uniform numbers — and desynchronises the two servers' streams after the first roll.

The vectors are generated against libstdc++ specifically, inside a container, because libc++ (what clang uses on macOS) implements uniform_int_distribution differently. The generator has an #error guard so it cannot be built against the wrong standard library by accident.

ZEROCASE: SHA1Interleave skips leading zero bytes of the shared secret S. The obvious implementation is correct about 255 times out of 256 and fails whenever S happens to begin with a zero byte — an intermittent login failure that is very hard to trace. ZEROCASE is a handshake constructed so that S starts with 0x00, and a test asserts the correct answer genuinely differs from the naive one.
